evidence: src/application/services/CancelBookingService.ts: in cancel(), `if (booking === undefined) throw new HttpError(404, `No booking ${bookingId}`);` sets an HTTP status code, which is a transport concern that belongs to the presentation layer.
The rest of cancel() is valid application orchestration: bookings.findById, booking.cancel(), payments.refund, bookings.save, notifications.send and toBookingView, all called through ports.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of CancelBookingService is normal use-case orchestration for an application layer. It loads the booking through a repository port and calls the domain behaviour booking.cancel(). It refunds through the PaymentGateway port, saves, notifies through the NotificationSender port and maps the result to a view. One part is out of place. In cancel(), the missing-booking case throws HttpError(404, ...), so the service decides the HTTP status code. Turning an outcome into an HTTP status is a transport concern that belongs to the presentation layer (the inbound HTTP adapter). The application layer should signal a transport-neutral error, such as BookingNotFound, and let the inbound adapter turn it into a 404. The import of HttpTypes from adapters/inbound is an import-direction issue, which is out of scope here. The finding is only about the transport responsibility being carried in this file.
